补库需求或支撑油价维持高位。当前欧洲天然气库存水平达75%，相比历史 平均水平低15%，瑞银预计冬季后库存水平或达15-33%，或支撑2027 年JKM均价于16美元/百万英热。我们认为油公司或仍具有配置价值，高油 价或带动新奥股份/宝丰能源的盈利改善。 推荐需求稳定且不惧油价下跌的产品 产业链角度，我们观察到PX/纯苯等上游产品库存普遍处于历史底部水平， 但中间和下游化工品（如涤纶长丝、钛白粉）库存处于正常或中高水平。我 们看好2027年下游需求稳健的化工品或受益于补库需求。2026年国内纺服 需求增长转正，涤纶长丝行业协同效果显著，我们预计2027年产业链盈利 或继续复苏且向下游转移，氨纶景气度也有望受纺服需求带动。改性塑料需 求或更受益于油价下跌，且下游库存也处于较低水平。 化工新材料增长趋势不变，关注农化周期反转 我们从两个维度判断周期复苏的可见性：1）当前价差处于历史底部；2）需 求有潜在改善的可能性。我们认为2027年年中农药化肥或开启复苏通道， 一方面其价差已处于过去五年的5%以下分位，另一方面厄尔尼诺有望支 撑2028年景气度。此外我们仍看好化工新材料或受益于AI下游需求增长，并 推荐业绩兑现较好的化工新材料厂商。 四大推荐投资主题 上半年油气价格或维持高位，我们推荐新奥股份、昆仑能源，此外需求稳定 且有出口需求的产品或受益于补库需求，推荐金发科技（加入亚太Key Call 名单）、桐昆股份、万华化学；下半年关注周期有望复苏的产品：如华鲁恒 升；此外我们认为AI相关的化工新材料企业估值已具备吸引力，如三环集 团、广钢气体、东材科技。 本证券研究报告由瑞银证券有限责任公司编制. 分析师声明及要求披露的项目，包括UBS(瑞银)发布的有关Quantitative Research 份、昆仑能源、金发科技、龙佰集团的目标价。我们用PE估值法得出三环集团的目标价。 我们用PEG估值法给东材科技估值。我们用可比公司的P/BV-ROE估值法给桐昆股份估值。 油气板块风险包括：1）原油价格下跌或者波动的风险；2）增储上产不及预期风险；3） 主要石化产品价格下跌的风险。 化工板块风险包括：1）国际油价大幅波动，带来盈利大幅波动的风险；2）全球经济增 长的不确定性，给化工需求带来的风险；3）新产能投产进度快于预期，导致化工景气度 大幅下降。 化工新材料板块风险包括：1）新材料行业技术尚未成熟，因此面临技术路线替代风 险；2）新材料行业处于发展初期，公司较依赖政策支持，因此面临政策风险；3）新材 料行业的收入和销量增长通常较难跟踪，行业增长的波动性较大。 中国油气化工行业2026 年 11 月 13 日 abc 33 要求披露 reports.stext: 印尼煤炭：政府释放70%收益分成信号，细则未明 瑞银 UBS · 印尼煤炭 印尼煤炭：政府释放70%收益分成信号，细则未明 Government indicates 70% earnings sharing; details remain unclear 机构： UBS（PT UBS Sekuritas Indonesia） ｜ 日期： 2026-11-16 ｜ 页数： 15 ｜ 分析师：Timothy Handerson / Igor Putra / Ivan Reynaldo Sutheja 等 本页为研究学习笔记，观点归属原机构 UBS。 目录 Contents 政策事件：总统要求国家获取矿业收益的70% 执行范围不明：CCoW 与 IUPK/IUP 待遇或分化 盈利敏感性：70%情形下行业净利润约 -36% 政府可能的三条路径与估值/风险 Key Takeaways · 核心观点 政策突袭：国家分成底线 70%，落地细节与机制均未公布 据 Reuters 与印尼本地媒体报道，总统 Prabowo Subianto 指示能源部长确保国家从矿业许可（IUP）中获取 至少 70% 的经济收益 ，必要时政府可直接入股，同时仍对私人投资保持开放。 该表态令市场与分析师意外：UBS 与其交流的本地矿商此前均不知情。在实施细则出台前，UBS 不急于下结论 ，仅给出情景测算。 基于 9M26 财报，覆盖的印尼煤炭公司目前通过权利金、税收与央地分成，已向政府支付相当于 经调整营业利润的约 41-61% ；若政府分成提至 70%，行业合计净利润潜在下行约 -36% 。 概念上与今年早些时候提出后又放弃的"利润分成"方案类似（模仿油气行业的 cost recovery / gross split 机制）；CCoW 老矿协议持有者因"锁定条款 / lex specialis"特殊法地位， 可能比 IUPK/IUP 持有者更有抵御力 ，但无保证。 政府或有三条路径：①矿企与国家签联合经营/利润或收入分成协议；②提高权利金和/或出口关税；③加大国家持股、通过分红转移经济价值。 政策不确定性仍是矿业板块的近期压制因素 。 Section 01 政策事件：总统要求国家获取矿业收益的70% 70% state take over mining economics 据 Reuters 与本地媒体报道，总统 Prabowo Subianto 指示能源部长确保国家从印尼矿业许可（IUP）的经济收益中获取 至少 70% ，并称政府可在必要时 直接持有矿业股权 ，同时仍对私人投资保持开放。消息一出令市场意外——UBS 与被访的本地矿商事先均不知情。UBS 因此不据此调整评级或目标价，仅做情景测算，等待执行细节。 这一"70%国家分成"概念并非全新：今年早些时候政府曾提出类似的利润分成（profit sharing）方案，试图把油气行业的 cost recovery / gross split 财政框架移植到矿业，但后来放弃。从 Figure 1 的政策清单看，印尼矿业政策工具箱里的多数加税类工具（权利金上调、出口税、暴利税、利润分成机制） 截至 2026 年 9 月均处于"已取消（Cancelled）"状态 ；已落地的包括 RKAB 配额削减（2026 年初，对镍矿供给收紧影响"高"）、HPM 定价公式（2026-04-15 生效）与矿业承包商使用法（2026 年 9 月签署）等，DSI 集中出口机构处于二期推进阶段。 Fig 1 · 印尼矿业政策进展一览（截至2026年9月，含已取消的权利金上调/出口税/暴利税/利润分成机制）| Summary of Indonesia mining policy development — Source: Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (ESDM), UBS（UBS Indonesia Coal p2） Section 02 执行范围不明：CCoW 与 IUPK/IUP 待遇或分化 Scope of implementation remains unclear 总统表态指向 整个矿业板块 ，但 UBS 认为实际执行范围存疑： CCoW（Coal Contract of Work，第一代工作合同）持有者可能相对更有抵御力 ，因为 CCoW 属于"锁定条款（nail-down）/ 特别法（lex specialis）"性质——合同条款具有准法律地位，单方面改动难度大；而 IUPK/IUP 许可持有者受政策变动的影响更直接。不过 UBS 强调这一点 并无保证 ，最终要看细则。 要点： 70% 如何计算、政府收入的构成清单均未公布。不同许可证结构（CCoW vs IUPK/IUP）、不同机制下，各公司实际盈利影响将差异显著。 Section 03 盈利敏感性：70%情形下行业净利润约 -36% Net profit sensitivity to the 70% scenario 以 9M26 财报为基础（经调整营业利润=收入-不含权利金的营业成本），UBS 覆盖的印尼煤炭公司当前 已向政府支付其经调整营业利润的约 41-61% （权利金+税收+央地分成），净利润相当于经调整营业利润的约 39-59%。若假设政府部分提升至约 70%，行业合计净利润潜在下行约 -36% 。 分公司的 9M26 数据（US$ mn）：行业合计收入 8,243、经调整营业利润 3,051；政府当前所得 1,618（占收入 20%、占经调整营业利润 53%）；矿企净利润 1,436（占收入 17%、占经调整营业利润 47%）。70% 情景下的潜在净利润冲击： AADI -35%、ADMR（仅炼焦煤）-49%、ITMG -22%、PTBA -37%、合计 -36%（-518 百万美元） 。ADMR 弹性最大（当前政府所得仅占其经调整营业利润的 41%），ITMG 最小（当前已达 61%）。 Fig 2 · 煤炭矿企对"政府获取70%经济收益"情景的净利润敏感性（9M26，US$ mn）| Coal miners net profit sensitivity to a 70% government economic benefit scenario — Source: Company data, UBS estimates（UBS Indonesia Coal p2） 评级与目标价（2026-11-13 收盘价）： AADI 买入、PT Rp16,000（现价 Rp10,700）； ADMR 买入（CBE）、PT Rp2,700（Rp1,335）； ADRO 买入、PT Rp3,500（Rp2,480）； PTBA 买入、PT Rp4,000（Rp3,200）； ITMG 买入、PT Rp30,000（Rp24,350）。 Section 04 政府可能的三条路径与估值/风险 Three routes, valuation methods and risks UBS 认为政府若推进，可能有三条路径提高国家在矿业经济中的份额： ① 联合经营 / 分成协议 ：矿企与国家签联合经营（joint operation）或利润/收入分成协议； ② 提高权利金和/或出口关税 ：直接加税类工具（但相关税种多数在 9 月前已被取消）； ③ 加大国家持股 ：政府增持矿业项目或矿企股权，通过分红把更多经济价值转移给国家。 实际盈利影响取决于最终机制、是否推进以及各公司的许可证结构。估值方法上：AADI 用 SOTP（动力煤主业 DCF，WACC 12.9%）；ADMR 用 SOTP（炼焦煤 DCF WACC 13.2% + 电解铝 DCF WACC 8.3%）；ADRO 用 SOTP（采矿承包、炼焦煤、铝、可再生能源 DCF + 所持 AADI 15% 股权按 Rp14,000/股估值）；ITMG 与 PTBA 用 DCF 并以短期倍数交叉验证。主要风险：煤价/铝价下跌、产销量不及预期、成本（权利金/燃油）上升，以及印尼矿业政策的不利变动。 结论： 在细则公布前，UBS 维持覆盖标的评级不变，但提示 政策不确定性是印尼矿业板块的近期 overhang ；70% 情景仅为敏感性参考，非基准假设。 本页为原文精读笔记，仅供研究参考、不构成投资建议；观点与数据归属原机构 UBS（PT UBS Sekuritas Indonesia）。原文版权归 UBS 所有。
reports.ftext: ab 16 November 2026 Global Research Indonesia Coal Sector Government indicates 70% earnings sharing; details remain unclear Indonesia signals greater state participation in mining Reuters and a local article reported that President Prabowo Subianto instructed the Energy Minister to ensure the state captures at least 70% of the economic benefits from Indonesia's mining permits (IUPs), adding that the government could take equity stakes where necessary while remaining open to private investment. The announcement appears to have come as a surprise: neither we nor the local miners we spoke with were aware of the proposal. We therefore refrain from drawing firm conclusions pending implementation details. Scope of implementation remains unclear The 70% concept is reminiscent of the profit sharing proposal floated earlier this year but subsequently abandoned, as the government previously tried to remodel the fiscal structure for mining sector after the already established cost recovery / gross split mechanism from oil and gas sector. Scope of implementation is also unclear - while the President's remarks indicate implementation for the entire mining sector, we believe miners under CCoW could potentially be more insulated relative to IUPK/IUP permit holders, given a nail-down / lex spesialis nature of the former, though there are no guarantees. Earnings risk if implemented? There have been no details on how the 70% would be calculated, nor do we have an exhaustive list of what constitutes government revenues. Based on information available to us in the financial statements as of 9M26, coal miners under our coverage currently pay ~41-61% of their adjusted operating profit (defined as revenues minus operating costs ex royalties) to government through royalties, taxes, and state/regional government profit sharing. Miners' net profit culminates to ~39-59% of adjusted operating profit. Assuming a scenario where government's portion is increased to ~70%, we estimate a potential ~36% downside to aggregate net profit of coal miners under our coverage. Details in Figure 2Coal m iners net profit sensitivity to a 70% governm ent econom ic benefit scenario. Policy uncertainty remains a near-term overhang for mining sector We see three potential routes for the government to capture a greater share of mining economics: 1) joint operation or profit/revenue sharing agreements between miners and the state; 2) higher royalties and/or export duties; and 3) greater state ownership in mining projects or miners, with dividends transferring more of the economic value to the government. The actual earnings impact will vary depending on the mechanism, if the government decides to push through, and will also vary by company and license structure. We see policy uncertainty to remain as a near-term overhang for the sector. This report has been prepared by PT UBS Sekuritas Indonesia. ANALYST CERTIFICATION AND REQUIRED DISCLOSURES, including information on the Quantitative Research Review published by UBS, begin on page 4. Equities Indonesia Coal Timothy Handerson Analyst timothy.handerson@ubs.com +62-21-2553 7933 Igor Putra Analyst igor.putra@ubs.com +62-21-2554 7033 Ivan Reynaldo Sutheja Analyst ivan-reynaldo.sutheja@ubs.com +62-21-2554 7037 Myles Allsop Analyst myles.allsop@ubs.com +44-20-7568 1693 Daniel Major Analyst daniel.major@ubs.com +44-20-7568 3472 Sharon Ding Analyst sharon.ding@ubs.com +852-2971 6284 Elvis Liu Analyst elvis.liu@ubs.com +852-3712 3052 Robin Chen Associate Analyst robin.chen@ubs.com +852-2971 8678 Indonesia Coal Sector 16 November 2026 ab 2 Indonesia Coal Sector UBS Research key charts Figure 1: Summary of Indonesia mining policy development Summar y of Indonesia mining policy devel opment Source: Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (ESDM), UBS Figure 2: Coal miners net profit sensitivity to a 70% government economic benefit scenario Coal miners net profit sensitivity to a 70% government economic benefit scenario Source: Company data, UBS estimates Indonesia Coal Sector 16 November 2026 ab 3 Valuation Method and Risk Statement ADMR: Our PT is based on a SOTP model: (1) we value the coking coal business using DCF with WACC assumption of 13.2% and LTG of 0%, and (2) the aluminium business based on DCF with WACC assumption of 8.3% and LTG assumption of 0%, with no additional capacity assumed beyond its 1st phase of 500ktpa. Key downside risks would be lower commodity prices, mainly coking coal and aluminium. ITMG: We use a DCF methodology, sense-checked against short-term multiples, to value ITMG. ITMG is exposed to a number of risks related to commodity cycles. Primarily this is the risk of material swings in underlying thermal coal prices impacting CF. Pricing levels also have an impact on investment decisions and returns. China is the biggest demand driver for global commodities in general. For thermal coal specifically, it is more than 90% self-sufficient but still represents an important swing factor for seaborne trade (of which Indonesia represents more than one-third). Policy is another risk as changes in rules, regulations, taxation and licencing around the mining industry, which is politically sensitive, can have unforeseeable impact on participating companies. PTBA: The sector is exposed to a number of risks related to the commodities cycle. Primarily this is the risk of material swings in underlying thermal coal prices impacting cash-flows. Pricing levels also have an impact on investment decisions and returns. China is the biggest demand driver for global commodities in general. For thermal coal specifically it is >90% self- sufficient, but still represents an important swing factor for the seaborne trade (of which Indonesia represents >1/3). Policy is another risk as changes in rules, regulations, taxation and licensing around the mining industry, which is politically sensitive, can have unforeseeable impacts on participating companies. We use DCF, sense-checked against short-term multiples, to value PTBA. ADRO: Our PT for Alamtri Resources (ADRO) is based on SOTP: 1) DCF (a 13.2% WACC) for the mining contracting business; 2) DCF for the coking coal business (a 13.2% WACC), applying a 30% holding discount; 3) DCF for the aluminium business (a 8.3% WACC), applying a 30% holding discount; 4) DCF for the upcoming renewables buisness ( a 7% WACC); and 5) fair value of its c15% stake in AADI at Rp14,000/share. Risks for ADRO are: 1) lower coking coal/aluminium prices; and 2) delays at its growth driver projects (aluminium/ solar farms/hydro power plants). AADI: Our valuation for AADI is derived using sum-of-the-parts methodology, with the core thermal coal business valued using DCF (12.9% WACC, no terminal growth). Potential risks to our Buy rating and Rp14,000 price target include: 1) a significant decline in coal prices; 2) lower-than-expected production/sales volume; 3) higher-than-expected costs (eg, royalties, fuel prices); and 4) adverse changes to Indonesia's mining regulations. reports.stext: 印尼金属：70%收益分成——标题冲击还是盈利现实？ 瑞银 UBS · 印尼金属 印尼金属：70%收益分成——标题冲击还是盈利现实？ 70% earnings sharing: headline or earnings reality? 机构： UBS（PT UBS Sekuritas Indonesia） ｜ 日期： 2026-11-16 ｜ 页数： 12 ｜ 分析师：Igor Putra / Timothy Handerson / Ivan Reynaldo Sutheja 等 本页为研究学习笔记，观点归属原机构 UBS。 目录 Contents 政策事件：总统要求国家获取矿业收益的70%，矿商措手不及 拆解"70%"：计入什么、覆盖哪些牌照、国家持股算不算 监管三条路径与覆盖标的评级/目标价 估值方法与风险提示 Key Takeaways · 核心观点 标题可能压制印尼金属股，但细节不足以量化影响 据 Reuters 及本地媒体报道，总统 Prabowo Subianto 指示能源部长确保国家从印尼矿业许可（IUP）的经济收益中获取 至少 70% ，必要时政府可直接入股，同时仍对私人投资保持开放。 UBS 认为这一标题 可能压制印尼金属板块股价 ——市场担忧矿商未来经济利益的不确定性；但目前细节太少， 无法量化实际盈利影响 ，最终影响取决于"70% 经济收益"如何定义、哪些采矿/冶炼牌照落入范围。 消息令市场意外（14 Nov 总统在 Palu Muhammadiyah 114 周年活动上表态），UBS 与本地矿商事前均不知情， 不急于下结论 ；概念上类似今年早些时候提出后又放弃的利润分成方案。 三个关键问题：①70% 计入哪些项目（权利金/出口税/所得税/央地分成/股利）——按 2025 年数据，不含股利时 没有一家金属矿商达到 70% ，含股利后国企 INCO、ANTM 达到或超过 70%；②范围是否仅限 IUP（还是含 IUI/CoW）——若仅限 IUP， 金/铜相对敞口小、镍敞口大 ；③既有国家持股是否计入 70%。 政府可能有三条路径：联合经营/利润或收入分成协议；提高权利金和/或出口关税；加大国家持股、以股利转移经济价值。在定义、范围与实施细则明确前， 政策不确定性（而非可量化的盈利下调）是板块的近期 overhang 。 Section 01 政策事件：总统要求国家获取矿业收益的70%，矿商措手不及 Indonesia signals greater state participation in mining 据 Reuters 与本地媒体报道，总统 Prabowo Subianto 于 11 月 14 日在 Palu 的 Muhammadiyah 114 周年活动上指示能源部长，确保国家从印尼矿业许可（IUP）的经济收益中获取 至少 70% ，并表示政府可在必要时 直接持有股权 ，同时仍对私人投资保持开放。UBS 认为该标题 可能在情绪上压制印尼金属股 ，因为投资者担心矿商未来的经济利益分配；但细节过于有限，尚无法量化影响。 消息显然出乎市场意料： UBS 及其交流的本地矿商事前均不知情 ，因此在实施细则出台前 UBS 不下硬结论。值得注意的是，"70%"概念令人联想到 今年早些时候提出、随后放弃的利润分成（profit sharing）提案 。生产/利润分成机制在印尼油气行业是成熟安排，但历史上 从未以同样方式应用于非能源矿业 。 要点： 同日 UBS 还发布了印尼 煤炭 版姊妹报告（Indonesia Coal Sector Earnings Sharing），给出行业敏感性测算（70% 情形行业净利润约 -36%）；本篇金属版因金属矿商的牌照结构与政府持股差异更大，UBS 选择 只做框架分析、不做量化 。 Section 02 拆解"70%"：计入什么、覆盖哪些牌照、国家持股算不算 Reading between the lines: what could the 70% actually capture? 问题一 · 哪些项目计入 70%？ 候选构成：权利金（royalties）、出口关税（export duties）、公司所得税、央地利润分成（regional/central government profit sharing）和/或股利（dividends）。按 2025 年各项贡献测算（ 不含股利 ）： 没有一家金属矿商达到 70% 门槛 ；若把股利计入，国企 INCO（买入）与 ANTM（买入）达到或超过 70% ——这意味着对国企而言，"已上缴的部分"可能已接近目标，增量负担取决于口径。 问题二 · 适用范围：仅 IUP，还是含 IUI 与 CoW？ 若 70% 目标 仅限 IUP ，则金/铜矿商相对敞口较小： BRMS（中性） 在 CoW 下运营； EMAS / 6228.HK（买入） 大部分在 CoW/IUI 下；UNTR（买入）旗下的 Martabe 金矿在 CoW 下； AMMN（买入） 的铜冶炼厂与贵金属精炼厂在 IUI 下。而 镍 可能面临更大敞口： ANTM 与 INCO 的 IUP 占比高 ； NCKL（买入）与 MBMA（买入） 因 IUI 敞口更大而相对防御。 问题三 · 既有国家持股是否计入？ 印尼政府本来就持有多家矿商股权。若 现有国家持股的价值/分红计入 "70% 经济收益"，则增量负担大幅下降；若只算新增上缴，冲击显著更大。这将直接决定实际增量的规模。 要点： 同一句"70%"在三种不同口径下，对各公司的盈利影响将 差异巨大 ——牌照结构（IUP/CoW/IUI）、是否含股利、是否计入既有国家持股，每一项都足以改变结论方向。 Section 03 监管三条路径与覆盖标的评级/目标价 What could change on the regulatory front? 尽管细节稀少，UBS 认为政府提高国家在矿业经济中份额的路径可能有三条： ① 联合经营 / 分成协议 ：矿企与国家签联合经营（joint-operation）或利润/收入分成安排； ② 提高权利金和/或出口关税 ：直接加税类工具； ③ 加大国家持股 ：政府增持矿业项目或矿企股权，通过股利把更多经济价值转移给政府。 最终盈利影响将因公司与牌照结构而 显著分化 。在政府明确 70% 的定义、范围与实施细则之前，UBS 预计 政策不确定性（而非可量化的盈利下修）构成板块的近期 overhang 。 公司 代码 评级 股价（2026-11-13 收盘） Amman Mineral Internasional AMMN.JK 买入（CBE） Rp3,680 Aneka Tambang ANTM.JK 买入 Rp2,810 Bumi Resources Minerals BRMS.JK 中性（CBE） Rp348 Merdeka Battery Materials MBMA.JK 买入（CBE） Rp338 Merdeka Gold Resources EMAS.JK 买入 Rp5,175 Merdeka Gold Resources 6228.HK 买入 HK$21.80 Trimegah Bangun Persada NCKL.JK 买入 Rp745 United Tractors UNTR.JK 买入 Rp24,975 Vale Indonesia Tbk INCO.JK 买入 Rp3,690 Source: UBS Global Research; LSEG Eikon。CBE = Core Banding Exception（高波动个股评级带宽豁免）；UBS 持有 AMMN、MBMA、UNTR ≥0.5% 长仓。 Section 04 估值方法与风险提示 Valuation methods and risk statement UBS 对各标的的估值方法： INCO SOTP（逐项目 DCF，合资项目按执行风险给予项目折价，上游低于下游）； UNTR SOTP（含煤炭开采承包等业务）； BRMS SOTP（在产资产 DCF + 非在产资产 EV/储量、EV/资源量全球对标折价）； ANTM SOTP（并表项目 DCF，合资按目标 P/BV，资源量按 1% 回收率折现）； NCKL SOTP（逐项目 DCF）； MBMA SOTP； EMAS/6228.HK 用 2028E PE； AMMN SOTP。 主要风险提示： 镍板块 ：镍价不及预期、印尼镍供给超预期、NPI 转化冰铜（matte）顺利推进、政府许可发放延迟、HPAL 项目（尤其印尼）加速投产、废钢对镍单位用量替代加快、中国需求走弱、芯片短缺恶化拖累电动车供给并降低镍需求、非煤电源冶炼镍的 ESG 压力、印尼禁止新建非电池级镍冶炼产能扩张。 金板块 ：金的权利金税率上调、出口关税落地、设价格上限的国内市场义务（DMO）、天气不利、品位低于预期、采矿剥离推迟、能源与融资成本上升。 公司层面 ：如 ANTM 黄金交易纠纷败诉（潜在罚金 Rp1.1tn）、NCKL Obi 镍钴 HPAL 项目的爬坡/成本风险、EMAS 山区开采作业难度与 RKAB 配额政策不确定性、AMMN 冶炼厂爬坡与 Elang 可研风险等。 结论： 在细则公布前，UBS 不据此调整评级与目标价，维持覆盖标的评级不变；提示 政策不确定性是印尼金属板块的近期 overhang ，后续关注 70% 的定义口径、牌照范围与既有国家持股的处理方式。 本页为原文精读笔记，仅供研究参考、不构成投资建议；观点与数据归属原机构 UBS（PT UBS Sekuritas Indonesia）。原文版权归 UBS 所有。
reports.ftext: ab 16 November 2026 Global Research Indonesia Metals 70% earnings sharing: headline or earnings reality? Indonesia signals greater state participation in mining Reuters and a local article reported that President Prabowo Subianto instructed the Energy Minister to ensure the state captures at least 70% of the economic benefits from Indonesia's mining permits (IUPs), adding that the government could take equity stakes where necessary while remaining open to private investment. We think the headline could weigh on Indonesian metals equities given uncertainty over miners' future economics, although details remain too limited to quantify the impact. Importantly, we think the eventual implications depend on what constitutes the 70% economic benefits and which mining/processing licences fall within its scope. Miners caught by surprise; details remain scarce The President made the remarks at Muhammadiyah's 114th anniversary event in Palu on 14 Nov. The announcement appears to have come as a surprise: neither we nor the local miners we spoke with were aware of the proposal. We therefore refrain from drawing firm conclusions pending implementing details. Notably, the 70% concept is reminiscent of the profit-sharing proposal floated earlier this year but subsequently abandoned (see Figure 3 for multiple policy headwinds announced). While production/profit-sharing mechanisms are established in Indonesia's oil and gas sector, they have not historically been applied in the same manner to non-energy mining. Reading between the lines: what could the 70% actually capture? We see three questions. First, what counts towards the 70%: royalties, export duties, corporate income tax, regional/central government profit sharing and/or dividends? Based on 2025 contributions from royalties, duties, taxes and profit sharing, but excluding dividends, none of the metal miners reached the 70% threshold. Including dividends, SOEs such as INCO (Buy) and ANTM (Buy) met/exceeded 70%. Second,does the threshold apply only to IUPs, or also industry licences (IUIs) and Contract of Works (CoWs)? If limited to IUPs, gold/copper could be relatively less exposed: BRMS (Neutral) operates under CoW; EMAS/6228.HK (Buy) largely under CoW/IUI; Martabe, owned by UNTR (Buy), is under CoW; and AMMN's (Buy) copper smelter and precious-metals refinery under IUI. Nickel could face greater exposure given ANTM's and INCO's IUP- heavy operations, while NCKL (Buy) and MBMA (Buy) could be relatively less exposed given their greater IUI exposure. Third, whether existing state ownership itself counts towards the targeted economic benefit will be important in determining the incremental burden. What could change on the regulatory front? While details remain scarce, we see three potential routes for the government to capture a greater share of mining economics: 1) joint-operation or profit/revenue-sharing arrangements between miners and the state; 2) higher royalties and/or export duties; and 3) greater state ownership in mining projects or miners, with dividends transferring more of the economic value to government. The eventual earnings impact could therefore vary materially by company and licence structure. Until the government clarifies the definition, scope and implementation of the 70% target, we expect policy uncertainty, rather than quantifiable earnings revisions, to be the near-term overhang. This report has been prepared by PT UBS Sekuritas Indonesia. ANALYST CERTIFICATION AND REQUIRED DISCLOSURES, including information on the Quantitative Research Review published by UBS, begin on page 4. Equities Indonesia Mining & Metals Igor Putra Analyst igor.putra@ubs.com +62-21-2554 7033 Timothy Handerson Analyst timothy.handerson@ubs.com +62-21-2553 7933 Ivan Reynaldo Sutheja Analyst ivan-reynaldo.sutheja@ubs.com +62-21-2554 7037 Daniel Major Analyst daniel.major@ubs.com +44-20-7568 3472 Lachlan Shaw Analyst lachlan.shaw@ubs.com +61-3-9242 6387 Sharon Ding Analyst sharon.ding@ubs.com +852-2971 6284 Myles Allsop Analyst myles.allsop@ubs.com +44-20-7568 1693 Indonesia Metals 16 November 2026 ab 2 Valuation Method and Risk Statement Risks to Indonesia’s nickel sector include, but are not limited to, lower-than-expected nickel prices, stronger nickel supply from Indonesia, successful nickel conversion from NPI into matte, delays to the Indonesian government’s nickel permit issuance, faster high-pressure acid leach (HPAL) project rollout, especially from Indonesia, faster-than-estimated usage of scrap for nickel units, lower metal demand from China, a worsening chip shortage resulting in lower EV supply and, in turn, lower nickel-unit demand, increasing enterprise awareness of ESG for nickel produced via non-coal power generation and Indonesia’s prohibition of new smelter expansion for non-battery grade nickel plants. Risks for Indonesia's gold sector include rising royalty rates for gold, export duty implementation, a domestic market obligation with a gold price cap, unfavourable weather dampening gold mining activity, lower gold grade than expected, longer mining pushback activity delaying gold output, higher input costs from the energy complex and higher funding costs than expected. INCO: We value INCO using an SOTP methodology, applying a DCF valuation methodology to each project, with an assumed expected mine life for each project. For JV projects, we assign a project discount for execution risks, with upstream JVs having lower risk than downstream. Downside risks include: 1) lower-than-expected nickel prices, given weaker global metal demand; 2) tighter-than-expected energy-complex supply driving higher coal and oil prices; 3) delayed downstream projects; 4) higher-than-expected Fed rate hikes; 5) failure to ramp up its HPAL project; and 6) failure to ramp up its FeNi project. UNTR: We derive our valuation based on SOTP. Downside risks include declining coal prices to a level lower than we forecast, a worsening investment appetite in the coal mining sector hampering heavy equipment demand, an accelerating mix of lower quality clients in Pama's portfolio, a widening gap between high calorific-value (CV) coal and low CV coal, an appreciating rupiah against the US dollar and declining coal miners' profitability leading to a reduction or cancellation of agreed-upon work within contractual terms. BRMS: We derive our SOTP valuation using DCF for the operating assets and EV/reserve and EV/resource valuation for the non-operating assets, based on those of global peers, with a valuation discount. Downside risks include: 1) lower-than-expected gold and copper prices; 2) higher-than-expected energy prices; 3) worse-than-expected Gorontalo Minerals drilling results, especially in the copper deposits; 4) slower-than-expected development of Gorontalo Minerals, Suma Heksa Sinergi and Linge Mineral Resources; and 5) a higher funding rate. Upside risks include: 1) higher-than-expected gold and copper prices; 2) lower-than-expected energy prices; 3) better-than-expected Gorontalo Minerals drilling results, especially in the copper deposits; 4) faster-than-expected development of Gorontalo Minerals, Suma Heksa Sinergi and Linge Mineral Resources; and 5) a lower funding rate. ANTM: We value ANTM using an SOTP methodology, applying a DCF valuation methodology to value each of the company's consolidated projects based on the expected mine life. We value JV projects by target P/BV, given limited financial disclosures. We value resources assuming they are all sold at the valuation date based on a 1% recovery rate. Downside risks include: 1) a lower nickel price than expected, given weaker global metal demand; 2) tighter energy complex supply than expected, raising coal and oil prices; 3) delayed downstream projects; 4) ANTM losing in its ongoing gold transaction dispute (a potential monetary penalty of Rp1.1tn); and 5) inability to secure electricity for new ferronickel capacity. NCKL: We value NCKL using an SOTP methodology, applying a DCF valuation methodology to each consolidated project by the expected mine life. Downside risks to our SOTP: 1) lower- than-expected nickel prices, given weaker global metal demand; 2) tighter-than-expected energy-complex supply driving higher coal and oil prices; 3) inability to convert nickel ore resources to reserves; 4) inability to source nickel ore with specific nickel content, given its limited mine life; 5) slower-than-expected ramp-up and/or higher-than-expected cost of its new HPAL project (Obi Nickel Cobalt; ONC); 6) transfer pricing and intragroup transaction risks; 7) volatile government regulations; 8) renewal or mining licence risks; and 9) risks of geological and natural disasters. MBMA: We value MBMA using an SOTP methodology. Downside risks include, but are not limited to: 1) Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) risks for Indonesia’s nickel; 2) technological risks resulting in the substitution of nickel; 3) resumption of carbon tax implementation; 4) transfer pricing and intragroup transaction risks; 5) nickel export sales tax and export ban risks; 6) FX risks; 7) exploration risks; 8) volatile government regulations; 9) renewal or mining license risks; 10) risks of geological and natural disasters; and 11) commodity pricing risks. Indonesia Metals 16 November 2026 ab 3 EMAS.JK / 6228.HK: We value the company via 2028E PE valuation. Downside risks include, but are not limited to: 1) a decline in commodity prices, especially gold prices; 2) the limited validity and extension option of its PETS licence; 3) export duty risk; 4) failure to secure funding; 5) uncertainty in mining quotas (RKAB) and related policies; 6) increasing challenges in its mining operations due to the mountainous topography; and 7) worse-than-expected permits for tailing capacity. AMMN: We derive our valuation based on sum-of-the-parts (SOTP) methodology.
